title: Token Flow Inkblot Lens — compact per-route/model performance canvas
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: High-level: design a compact, scan-friendly UI component (the 'Inkblot Lens') to surface per-route and per-model token-level performance signals in a single canvas. The lens purpose is to help engineers and SREs quickly understand token distribution, latency hotspots, throughput bands, and token-affinity anomalies for a given model route without leaving the list/detail context. The view must be dense, mobile-friendly for on-call use, and composable inside existing route cards and the model detail page.
design_goals: Distill token-level signals into a single compact canvas that fits on a route card (240–320px width)
Show both distribution (latency percentiles) and token-flow directionality in the same visual language
Allow instant filtering by time window and by token group (prompt/system/user/assistant)
Enable quick drill-through to full perf canvas and traces with 1 click
Prioritize readability for on-call and for product engineers reviewing regressions
proposed_components: Dual-sparkline stack: top = throughput heatband (requests/min, autoscaled bins), bottom = latency violin simplified to percentile ribbons
Token-flow glyph: small inkblot-shaped micrograph where left/right lobes indicate prompt vs. generated token ratios and color saturation encodes avg token latency
Affinity mini-map: 4-slot timeline showing token-group spikes (system, user, assistant, tools)
Interactive threshold overlay: adjustable P95/P99 markers with on-hover counts and sample links
Context pill: model name, route name, (pinned) rollout variant tag, and quick actions (open traces, open rollout)
prototype_notes: Prototype built with interactive states (hover, focus, time-range switch) in Figma; includes sample data sets for skewed prompt-heavy workloads and assistant-heavy workloads.
The inkblot glyph is computed client-side from a 5-value summary vector (prompt_tokens, gen_tokens, avg_latency, p95_latency, burstiness_score). Implementation approach documented in Confluence.
Hover on percentile ribbons shows numerical tooltip and links to top-3 sample traces (prepopulated IDs).
Clicking the mini-map opens the full model-route timeline in a right-hand drawer with microtrace playback.
Prototype demonstrates two density modes: compact (default) and expanded (for model detail page).
chart_spec_highlights: Throughput heatband: time bucket = 1m, smoothing = 3-bucket rolling median, color ramp = blues with log scale mapping to avoid washout
Latency ribbons: show 50/75/90/95/99 percentiles as layered translucent ribbons; vertical extent uses log-scaled ms axis
Inkblot glyph: normalized lobes using min-max scaling across selected time window; saturation corresponds to avg latency; outline stroke thickness maps to burstiness_score
Token affinity mini-map: discrete stacked bars per token-group with stacked value labels on hover; aggregation window = same as heatband
Threshold overlay: persistent P95 and P99 markers; adjustable by keyboard shortcuts; when exceeded shows red pulsing dot on route card
tradeoffs: Density vs. clarity: compact mode sacrifices exact numbers for glanceable shapes; expanded mode required for investigative work
Client calculation of inkblot glyph reduces API payload but adds CPU to client — tradeoff for offline-friendly browser caching
Percentile ribbons require careful color contrast to be readable at small sizes; chosen translucent layers mitigate but may be hard for colorblind users (see accessibility notes)
Embedding links to traces/sample requests increases surface area for data privacy — queries must honor project RBAC and sampling policies
accessibility_considerations: All critical information must be available via tooltip text and keyboard focus (no info encoded only in color)
Use patterns and textures for percentile ribbons in high-contrast mode
Inkblot glyph will have ARIA label with numeric summary fallback
Ensure target tap/click areas meet 44px minimum in compact mode via expanded hit targets (visual remains small but hit area larger)
acceptance_criteria: Compact lens implemented on route list cards and model detail header in expanded form
Engineering sign-off on client-side inkblot computation and agreed API shape (summary vector) — ENG-8921 updated
Design review complete with accessibility checklist and contrast tests
Automated visual regression snapshots for three canonical data shapes (prompt-heavy, assistant-heavy, bursty)
Product owner (PM) approves rollout gating and error-handling copy
